title: Quasi-coherent tensor precomposition invertible on an inverse-image open
statement: Let f:X→Y be any scheme morphism, with independently chosen ambient derived categories and derived categories of the over-sites on all opens [def-pc-derived-category]. Let L=derivedPullbackAcrossUniverses f [def-pc-derived-pullback-across-universes], P∈D_QCoh(X), I∈D(Y) perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], i:I→1_Y, and V⊆Y an open. Assume restriction of i to V is invertible. For the fixed derived tensor structure [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], there exists a unit isomorphism e:L(1_Y)≅1_X such that R=L(I)⊗P has quasi-coherent cohomology and j=(L(i)⊗id_P);(e⊗id_P);λ_P is invertible after restriction to f⁻¹(V). This assertion has no direct-image functor, adjunction or annihilation hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0E4G, Lemma 48.4.4, final projection-formula paragraph; perfect.tex, Tags 08DW, 08DX and 08EU

proof.text: Use the strong monoidal model of standard derived pullback and its inverse unit isomorphism. Localization.compUniqFunctor identifies the tensor unit (Qh of the degree-zero structure module) with the standard unit. Map this comparison by standard pullback and then the inverse standard equivalence; compose with the inverse equivalence unit. This constructs e in the specified independent universes.

Perfect I has quasi-coherent cohomology by lem-sc-perfect-qcoherent. Uniqueness of the localization lift of homology gives homologyComparison, so both directions of schemeDerivedStandardEquivalence preserve quasi-coherence. Apply standard derived pullback preservation and transport its conclusion back to X. Apply canonical_derivedTensor_preserve_QCoh with P.property.

An exact functor commutes with the unique standard localization comparisons: compare its Qh factorizations and descend the resulting natural isomorphism by full faithfulness of precomposition with Qh. Apply this to both over restriction functors. Transfer the assumption on i to standard restriction, compose restriction with the over-site equivalence, and use the natural standard open-restriction pullback comparison. Reflect invertibility through the derived over equivalence and the standard comparison to obtain invertibility of restricted L(i).

Construct a derived localization for the open subscheme, in the given over-site universe, by composing the complex over-site equivalence with the supplied localization; its universal property follows by transport along that equivalence. The natural derived tensor restriction comparison, evaluated at the fixed second factor P, is an isomorphism between tensorRight P followed by restriction and restriction followed by tensorRight of restricted P. NatIso.isIso_map_iff and reflection through the derived over equivalence show that restriction of L(i) whiskered by P is invertible. Finally, restriction preserves the isomorphisms e.hom whiskered by P and the left unitor. Functor.map_comp and the composition instance conclude that the displayed composite is invertible.

theorem exists_derivedTensor_precomposition_open
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ W : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over W))]
    [∀ W : Y.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over W))]
    (V : Y.Opens) (P : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X) (I : schemeDerivedCategory Y)
    (hI : Scheme.IsPerfect Y I) (i : I ⟶ 𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory Y))
    (hi : IsIso ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)
      V).mapDerivedCategory.map i)) :
    ∃ e : (derivedPullbackAcrossUniverses f).obj (𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory Y)) ≅
        𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory X),
      schemeDerivedQCohProperty X ((derivedPullbackAcrossUniverses f).obj I ⊗ P.obj) ∧
      IsIso ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        (f ⁻¹ᵁ V)).mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((derivedPullbackAcrossUniverses f).map i ▷ P.obj ≫
            e.hom ▷ P.obj ≫ (λ_ P.obj).hom))
